research_question: Does the repository's existing simple MA60 and 60-day-high volume breakout strategy produce a distinct historical path under the current VCP research universe, execution and cost contract?
hypothesis: A simple trend breakout is a useful null reference for strategy-level overlap. Similar results would weaken claims that the frozen VCP implementation adds distinct portfolio behavior; different results would justify an overlap audit, not prove that either method is superior.
unique_change: Use the existing trend_breakout strategy with all builtin defaults. Keep the 2016-2026 interval, Shanghai/Shenzhen historical union, open_t+1 execution, historical stamp tax, costs, four positions and equal sizing fixed.
decision_rules: Run the existing defaults once; do not vary the 60-day window, MA, volume ratio, stop, holding period, score or position count.
Report candidates, trades, timing violations, exposure, drawdown, payoff concentration and execution rejections before any overlap interpretation.
Do not treat the performance difference as isolated VCP structure alpha because the strategies also differ in filters, ranking and exits.
Only proceed to a descriptive P3 overlap audit if the run is causal and nonempty. Do not run a combined portfolio or allocation search on this exposed interval.
development_note: This is an exposed historical null reference using an existing strategy, not parameter optimization, independent validation, portfolio promotion or live qualification.
